statements.statement: Preliminary FY27 budget to be presented Feb 19 to finance committee will not be a balanced budget and will be reliant on an override.
Health insurance rate increase received for FY27 is 8.85%, though ongoing PEC negotiations could change that.
Additional undetermined factors could still affect the FY27 budget, including winding down TCP and potential changes to the recycling program.
The preliminary FY27 budget gap is looking to be over $3 million, to be confirmed once school numbers are finalized.
Preliminary free cash figure from the FY25 closeout is looking very healthy at over $3 million, boosted by school turnback and investment income.
The capital plan was conservatively budgeted assuming $1.8 million in free cash, well below the roughly $3 million now expected; the capital plan will not be revisited until final numbers are in.
With free cash running high, the town manager plans to make contributions into the stabilization fund and potentially the health insurance stabilization fund.
MUNIS costs, previously subsidized by ARPA during the cloud transition, are rising almost $50,000 for FY27 to a total of $108,000, partly offset by dropping ClearGov.
A warrant article proposes a multi-year allocation of $15,000 for the 300th anniversary committee, expected to be funded with free cash.
PAC's warrant article requests a sum of $209,000 from expected income as its operating budget appropriation.

A resident proposed raising the tax rate by about $1.89 per thousand instead of pursuing an override, arguing it would generate roughly $5 million and could have covered the town's and school's added costs and the current roughly $3 million gap.
